question: Should the current repair mutation guard architecture become the authoritative production boundary once the current-head `pnpm check` failure is resolved?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent but changes live merge, close, publication, authorization, and credential behavior across several repair phases, so accepting its fail-closed availability tradeoffs requires maintainer ownership.

options.title: Validate and land together
options.body: Resolve the current-head check failure, repeat focused exact-head validation, and land the shared guards and credential renewal as one coordinated safety change.

options.title: Split workflow credentials
options.body: Land the mutation-boundary code separately and move post-execution state-token renewal into a follow-up if maintainers want a narrower initial operational rollout.

options.title: Pause for staged rollout
options.body: Keep the draft open and introduce the guards behind a controlled repair-lane rollout if maintainers need production telemetry before making them authoritative.

recommendation.title: Validate and land together
recommendation.body: Resolve the current-head check failure, repeat focused exact-head validation, and land the shared guards and credential renewal as one coordinated safety change.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced both the merged reviewed-activity foundation and the current repair-boundary implementation, making them the best available owner for explaining and coordinating the rollout tradeoffs.
